The best meal of our lifetime so far!
Oct 2026 • Couples
This is truly, the best meal we have ever experienced. We love food and have dined a numerous Michelin restaurants around the world. But, TUNG is the most creative, unique, whimsical ding experience we have enjoyed. The meal was 17 course which, took you through the many layers of Vietnamese culture and through many regions. Each bite was meticulously prepared to awaken your inner spirit and teach you about the beautiful people and food of Vietnam. We had deconstructed pho, a sweet potato ‘pudding’ with hollandaise sauce which reminded us of a delicate crème brute. The wagu beef is grade 5. The meal was accented with fruits found in the region….salt and sweet permiated our delicious bites. I don’t want to give away too much. The surprise of each course is 1/2 the fun. Do not miss the opportunity to dine here. The wine pairing was spot on. And the restaurant team was especially talented and knowledgeable. I can’t say enough great adjectives to describe this gem. I’m so glad we found them. We will return!

An unforgettable dinner for two in Hanoi
Aug 2026 • Couples
We dined at T.U.N.G Dining at the end of July, as a couple, and it was one of the best moments of our trip. The tasting menu is incredibly creative: very visual plates, with perfectly balanced flavors, and contrasts of textures and temperatures that surprise with every bite. Local products are elevated there with true technical mastery.

The welcome is warm, the service attentive and precise, and the setting elegant and intimate. It is ideal for a romantic dinner. The drink pairings accompany the meal very well, and the price-quality ratio is justified for a restaurant of this level.

A must-visit address to discover Vietnamese gastronomy in a different way. We will return with pleasure. Remember to book well in advance!

Something truly special
Jun 2026 • Couples
The Michelin Guide absolutely gets this one right. Served in a beautifully choreographed sequence of courses, the menu takes you on a culinary journey across Vietnam, with the occasional detour into Japanese cuisine. It is an evening of constant discovery, where each dish feels like another stop on an expertly curated gastronomic itinerary.
Visually, every course is striking, while the quality of the ingredients is exceptional. At times, the execution and ambition are enough to make some European Michelin-starred restaurants look rather ordinary by comparison.

That said, the sheer number of dishes also reveals a few that simply aren’t necessary. One noodle course, in particular, felt as though it had somehow slipped into an otherwise spectacular table-side fireworks display. The menu could—and should—be tightened slightly. When every course is competing for attention, less can occasionally be more.

One thing I would recommend without hesitation, however, is the non-alcoholic pairing. There are very few restaurants where I would actively choose it over its alcoholic counterpart; this is one of them. The kombuchas are bold, sometimes challenging, but always exceptionally well balanced, with flavor profiles that complement the food rather than merely accompany it.

An unforgettable dinner, full of imagination, precision and genuine character. We won’t be forgetting this one anytime soon.

Keep going. This is something special.
